changed.title: A row OR spare on at all its missing singleton columns, at least two, is a gate outside the row ORs and their readers for incomparable rows
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool)
    (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit)
    (r : Fin n → Fin C.gates.length) (s : Fin n → ℕ) (v : Fin n),
  let gate := PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C
  let wire := fun idx : Fin C.gates.length => n + m + idx.val
  let reads := PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.readsIn C (Finset.range C.gates.length)
  let col := fun label : Fin m =>
    List.replicate n false ++ List.ofFn (fun b : Fin m => decide (b = label))
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n + m) C →
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C →
  (∀ u : Fin n, C.output ≠ u.val) →
  (∀ c, ∃ u, G u c = false) →
  (∀ u w, u ≠ w → ∃ c, G u c = true ∧ G w c = false) →
  (∀ u : Fin n, reads u.val = 1 ∧ (gate (r u).val).op = .or ∧
    ((gate (r u).val).inputs = [u.val, s u] ∨
      (gate (r u).val).inputs = [s u, u.val])) →
  2 ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun c => G v c = false)).card →
  (∀ c, G v c = false → (C.wires (col c)).getD (s v) false = true) →
  ∃ j : Fin C.gates.length, s v = wire j ∧
    ∀ w, j ≠ r w ∧ wire (r w) ∉ (gate j.val).inputs
changed.unlocks: one step of the general count of two gates a row on the one-a-side promise, the gate found outside the row gates; it moves no bound by itself
changed.context: On paper. A column alone gives output zero. On a neighbor of row w its OR must be off there, since turning on w changes the output through that OR. The chosen spare is on at two singleton columns, so it is a gate. If it equals a row OR or reads one by OR, the chosen row OR is on throughout that other row, contradicting row distinction by domination. If it reads a row OR by AND, that OR is on at every column missing the chosen row. Its own neighbors must then lie inside the chosen row. Equality of row indices would give a cycle in each case. Companions cannot exist: it is about every graph.

changed.title: The two-lit function of the graph H on 6 points with mask 270585271 on shared wires has an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 8 gates
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 8 ∧ ∀ i j : Fin 6, C.eval (List.ofFn fun k : Fin 6 => decide (k = i ∨ k = j)) = (270585271 : ℕ).testBit (6 * min i.val j.val + max i.val j.val)
changed.unlocks: the exact size of the two-lit-points function of this graph on six shared wires; the family shows where a NOT gate pays with no equal lines
changed.sketch: We hold a circuit of 9 gates, a weak hand form (best over a few point orders and the complement plus a NOT, equal gates merged): OR(0,1), NOT(6), AND(5,7), OR(4,6), AND(3,9), AND(2,4), OR(8,10), OR(11,12), NOT(13) (inputs 0-5 are the points, gate k is wire 6 + k, output last). We hold no circuit of 8 gates; this is a search. No complete search of ours has run at six points.

changed.title: An AND/OR circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 53 gates computes the edge function of the listed graph on 24 vertices with 44 edges
changed.unlocks: one search on a named graph: is there a circuit one gate smaller than the best we know for its edge function; a found circuit is a bound from above, a proof of none a bound from below
changed.context: SKETCH: truth not known to us; the opposite row is offered beside it. Proved by exhibiting ONE circuit with at most the stated number of gates of fan-in at most two that computes the edge function (true exactly when both ends of some edge are true) on every input; checked by evaluation. The best circuit known to us has one gate more (computed, not checked). Size: minutes if such a circuit exists. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
